verses.1: He ruled for twenty-one years as king. Then, he ruled for fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
verses.2: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as the nations had done before the LORD, since the time when the LORD created Israel.
verses.3: And he sat down and built the altars where his father Jehoshua had been sacrificed. He also rebuilt the idols of the gods. He made offerings to all the nations in heaven, and he worshiped them.
verses.4: And He built the Temple of God in Jerusalem. For God said, “In Jerusalem, My name will be remembered forever.”
verses.5: And he made altars for all the nations of the heavens, in two courtyards of the house of Jehovah.
verses.6: And he brought his children to destruction through fire. He also created scorpions, snakes, and other harmful creatures. He made them do evil in the eyes of Jehovah, so that He would be angry.
verses.7: And he set up the ark of the covenant that he had made in the house of God. It was the ark that God told David and Solomon to place in this house. In Jerusalem, where I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will place my name above it.
verses.8: And I will not remove the feet of Israel from the land that I have given them, except if they keep doing everything that is commanded in all the Torah, laws, and regulations by Moses.
verses.9: And Manasseh made Judah and the people of Jerusalem do evil things, contrary to what the LORD had forbidden them from doing, as a punishment for their actions against the Israelites.
verses.10: And Jehovah spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they did not listen.
verses.11: And Jehovah brought upon them the leaders of the army who were under the rule of Assyria. He captured Manasseh in the wilderness and imprisoned him in chains. Then he threw him into the river.
verses.12: And he became like a disease to the face of Jehovah, his God. He was greatly ashamed before the gods of his ancestors.
verses.13: And he prayed to him, and begged for his help. God heard his prayer, and brought him back to his throne as king. Then Menashe knew that Jehovah was indeed the true God.
verses.14: And after that, he built a strong city for David’s kingdom, located near the river. He also built gates leading into the city, and he raised it very high. He placed soldiers in all the fortified cities of Judah.
verses.15: And he removed the idols of the Canaanites and all the idols from the house of Jehovah. He also destroyed all the altars that were built in the hill of Jehovah and in Jerusalem. He scattered them far away from the city.
verses.16: And he built an altar for Yahweh. He offered sacrifices and prayers on that altar. He said to the Jews, “Serve Yahweh, the God of Israel.”
verses.17: But still, the people worship in the temples only for their God, Yehovah.
verses.18: And also Menahe’s words and prayers to his God, as well as the words of the prophets who spoke to him in the name of Jehovah, the God of Israel. These are all related to the words of the kings of Israel.
verses.19: And his prayers, and all his sins, and all the places where he committed them during his death. The places where he built those structures, and the places where he set up those monuments in front of the captives. All these things are written down in the records of the judges.
verses.20: And Menashe lay with his fathers. He was buried in his house. And Amnon became king after him.
verses.21: He ruled for forty-two years. He was king in Jerusalem for forty-two years.
verses.22: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Manasseh had done. He also worshiped idols, just as his father Manasseh had done.
verses.23: And I will not submit to the Lord like Manasseh his father did. For Manasseh was a great sinner.
verses.24: And his servants bound him and killed him in his own house.
verses.25: And the people of the land killed all those who were against King Amon. Then, the people of the land made Yoash their king.
